argument_markdown:
## Source-backed inputs

ATT-0065, confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109, identifies the scheme-theoretic balanced CE evaluation-failure ideal with the relative Picard triviality locus, under the stated equation-bundle freeness/base-change hypothesis. ATT-0066, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116, constructs the Abel–Jacobi incidence and identifies ordering over its distinct-support open as a finite étale S_6-torsor without reducing only one side. ATT-0086, confirmed by REV-0135 and REV-0138, eliminates the h^0(L)=4 stratum and gives the P²-bundle over a reduced base under the weak normalization. ATT-0088, confirmed by REV-0139 and REV-0142, proves fibrewise nonemptiness of the distinct-support open, its smooth relative dimension two, the identification Z=Ord(U), and the regular codimension-four immersion Z→Conf_6(C/S). These inputs are used only within their verified scopes; in particular S is reduced and the weak normalization remains an explicit hypothesis.

## Proved steps

1. Since AJ is a projective-plane bundle over the integral scheme S, it is integral: locally on S it is P²×S. The same local description, together with normality of S and normality of polynomial rings and their localizations over a normal domain, shows that AJ is normal. The nonempty open U is therefore normal and integral. Its relative dimension over S is two, so dim(U)=dim(S)+2.

2. The verified incidence comparison gives a finite étale right G-torsor p:Z→U for G=S_6. Choose a geometric point u and a point of Z_u. This identifies Z_u with G. The π_1^{ét}(U,u)-action commutes with the right G-action, hence is left multiplication through a homomorphism ρ:π_1^{ét}(U,u)→G, well-defined up to conjugacy. Write H=im(ρ).

3. Connected components of a finite étale cover of the connected scheme U correspond to π_1^{ét}(U,u)-orbits in its geometric fibre. The orbits in G under left multiplication by H are the left cosets Hg. Hence Z has [G:H] connected components, and the fibre of each component has |H| points. Each component is consequently finite étale of degree |H| and surjective over U.

4. A finite étale scheme over normal U is normal. In a locally Noetherian normal scheme, irreducible components are pairwise disjoint and open-and-closed; therefore every connected component of Z is irreducible. Thus connected and irreducible components coincide and Irr(Z)=H\G. Finite morphisms preserve dimension, so every component has dimension dim(U)=dim(S)+2.

5. Right multiplication sends Hg to Hga, so the right G-action is transitive on Irr(Z), and the stabilizer of Hg is {a∈G: Hga=Hg}=g^{-1}Hg. The action on geometric points is free because Z→U is a G-torsor. Thus these are component stabilizers for the ordering action, not automorphism groups of pointed curves.

6. The regular codimension-four immersion is the verified smooth-over-S argument from ATT-0088: Z and Conf_6(C/S) are smooth over S of relative dimensions two and six, respectively, and Z is closed by its Fitting presentation. No conclusion is drawn from determinantal expected-codimension numerology.

## Computational hypotheses

None. No finite experiment or point count is used.

## Gaps and exact scope

The theorem leaves H undetermined and does not assert full S_6 monodromy. It assumes rather than proves normality or irreducibility of the balanced base. The trivial point stabilizer is only for the S_6 ordering action; Aut(C,Γ), Aut(C,γ,Γ), and moduli inertia are not computed. No morphism or closed embedding into M_{6,6}, no analysis of unbalanced CE strata, and no Hodge, Tate, Gysin, or RED-0001 conclusion is claimed.

## Blocked routes

The vcd-only-vanishing, undecorated-CGP graph-complex, point-count-without-parity-separation, and forgetful-map/local-system routes are not used. In particular the numerical value 21−17=4 is not promoted to a codimension or Gysin statement.

claims.justification: ATT-0065/REV-0108/REV-0109 supply the scheme-theoretic CE/Picard identification; ATT-0066/REV-0110/REV-0116 supply the Abel–Jacobi and torsor construction; ATT-0086/REV-0135/REV-0138 eliminate the jumping stratum; ATT-0088/REV-0139/REV-0142 supply nonemptiness, smoothness, the torsor identification, and regularity.
claims.statement: Under the theorem hypotheses, AJ is a P²-bundle, its distinct-support open U is nonempty and smooth surjective over S of relative dimension two, Z→U is a finite étale S_6-torsor of degree 720, and Z→Conf_6(C/S) is a regular immersion of pure codimension four.

claims.justification: A projective-plane bundle is locally P²×S, hence is normal and integral over a normal integral base; a nonempty open preserves both properties. Relative dimension two gives the dimension formula.
claims.statement: If S is normal integral, then U is normal integral and has dimension dim(S)+2.

claims.justification: Finite étale connected components are π_1^{ét}-orbits in the geometric fibre. Those orbits are the left H-cosets. Normality makes each connected component irreducible, and finiteness preserves dimension.
claims.statement: For H equal to the geometric monodromy image of the ordering torsor, Irr(Z) is H\S_6; hence the number of irreducible components is [S_6:H], every component has degree |H| over U and dimension dim(S)+2, and Z is irreducible exactly when H=S_6.

claims.justification: Right multiplication acts transitively on H\S_6 and elementary coset algebra gives the component stabilizer. Point stabilizers vanish by the defining freeness of an S_6-torsor.
claims.statement: The right S_6-action is transitive on Irr(Z); the stabilizer of the component Hg is g^{-1}Hg, while every geometric point has trivial stabilizer.

Expected determinantal codimension is not used to prove regularity; the regular immersion is imported only in its verified smooth-over-the-base form.
Connected components are upgraded to irreducible components only after imposing normality.
The balanced model is not treated as a closed locus in M_{6,6}, and the numerical difference 21−17=4 is not called a codimension there.
The free S_6-ordering action is not confused with Aut(C,Γ) or moduli inertia.

gap_markers: GAP-0099-1: The actual geometric monodromy subgroup H≤S_6 is not determined; no transposition or full-monodromy occurrence locus is proved.
GAP-0099-2: Normality and irreducibility of the actual balanced tetragonal base are not proved.

GAP-0099-4: No morphism, quasi-finiteness, closedness, purity, lci, codimension, or Gysin statement inside M_{6,6} is established.

novelty_claims: Over a normal integral balanced base, the previously known finite étale ordering torsor admits an exact irreducible-component formula Irr(Z)=H\S_6, with component degrees |H| and dimensions dim(S)+2.

The S_6-stabilizer of each irreducible component is identified as a conjugate of geometric monodromy H, while point stabilizers remain trivial; this cleanly separates ordering-action stabilizers from the still-unknown moduli inertia.
summary: The balanced ordered failure model has a complete conditional component formula over a normal integral base: its irreducible components are the monodromy cosets H\S_6, all have relative dimension two, and their S_6-stabilizers are conjugates of H. This does not compute the actual monodromy subgroup or moduli inertia.

theorem_scope.base: normal integral finite type over a characteristic-zero field
hypotheses: ambient equation-bundle finite local freeness and arbitrary base change

theorem_statement: Let S be a normal integral finite-type scheme over a characteristic-zero field, carrying a smooth proper genus-six family π:C→S and a finite flat degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl cover γ:C→P¹_S whose relations bundle is fibrewise O(4)⊕O(5). Assume the weak relative-canonical normalization on every geometric fibre and the finite-local-freeness and base-change hypothesis required for the ambient CE evaluation comparison. Let L=W_5⊗ω_{C/S}^{-1}; let AJ be the relative Abel–Jacobi incidence of effective degree-six divisors linearly equivalent to L; let U⊂AJ be the open locus of divisors with six distinct support points; and let Z⊂Conf_6(C/S) be the scheme-theoretic CE evaluation-failure locus. Then AJ is a P²-bundle over S, U is normal integral and smooth surjective over S of relative dimension two, and Z→U is the finite étale S_6-torsor of orderings, of degree 720. The immersion Z→Conf_6(C/S) is regular of pure codimension four. For a geometric point u of U, identify the right S_6-torsor Z_u with S_6 and let H≤S_6 be the image, defined up to conjugacy, of π_1^{ét}(U,u) acting by left translations. Then Irr(Z) is the transitive right S_6-set H\S_6: Z has exactly [S_6:H] irreducible components, every component is finite étale of degree |H| over U and has dimension dim(S)+2, and the stabilizer in S_6 of the component represented by Hg is g^{-1}Hg. The stabilizer of every geometric point for the torsor action is trivial. Thus Z is irreducible if and only if H=S_6. If dim(S)=15, every component has dimension 17; the equality 21−17=4 is only a numerical comparison and is not a codimension statement inside M_{6,6}.
